calculators.name: Multi-Spindle Machining - Bar Stock
calculators.description: The bar bought per part. The bar is the part's OD (or across flats) plus the stock allowance on each side, snapped up to the location's preferred size; each part takes its length, the parting tool's width (tblPartingRingWidth, by the bar's diameter) and the facing stock (minStockAllowance). A bar of standardStockLength yields as many parts as fit after the remnant the bar feeder cannot use, and each part carries its share of the whole bar. Priced per kg for the bar's form (material_stock_prices).

source.engine: part_length_mm (the part's length along its turning axis, CAD)
bar_section_area_mm2 (round: π/4 D²; hex: √3/2 AF²; square: AF²)
bar_remnant_mm (the bar end the feeder cannot use: 2-6 in is typical, 6 in taken; multi-spindle-research.ts)
price_per_kg (the bar form's price at the location, material_stock_prices)

fields.name: Parts per Bar
fields.formula: max(1, floor(({Bar Length} - {Bar Remnant}) / {Length per Part}))

calculators.name: Multi-Spindle Machining - Cycle
calculators.description: One part per index. Every station of the machine cuts at once, so the cycle is set by the slowest station (its operations, split across the spindles and their slides by the station plan, each with its tool positioning), plus the index: the drum turns, the part transfers to the back-work spindle, the bar feeds and the spindles synchronize.

source.engine: slowest_station_s (the longest station of the station plan)

fields.name: Index Time
fields.formula: {Drum Index Time} + {Transfer Time} + {Stock Feed Time} + {Speed Synchronization Time}
